adaptation: EncapsulatorP Atlas

records.boundary: This is a finite search for even totals from 20 through 200. Finding every pair in this range does not prove Goldbach’s conjecture.
adaptation: Enumerate all valid radii independently of animation frames.
Label 1 correctly as non-prime.
Fit the full number line to the viewport; add discrete step control.

records.boundary: The reset and counter are defined animation rules in arbitrary units. This is not a physical model, demonstrated monodromy or construction of Riemann sheets. “Bitemporal” preserves the supplied concept’s name.
adaptation: Replace hole-center claim with inner-rim location.
Replace physical units and monodromy claims with explicit arbitrary-unit reset rules.
Keep wireframe aligned with particle coordinates.
Reset event colors and honor reduced motion.

records.boundary: A finite parameter grid and transient cutoff can hide narrow windows or slow approach. Preset names orient the reader; the HUD gives sample counts rather than a hard-coded stability verdict.
adaptation: Remove hard-coded stability classifications.
Label recorded orbit by its actual iterations51–150.
Keep source sampling choices explicit; preserve bifurcation and orbit panels.

records.boundary: This is a toy inspired by Collatz-style branching. No physical relation to early dark energy or derived Poincaré return map is established. Staying within the sampled range is not a proof of boundedness.
adaptation: Replace unsupported cosmological labels with recurrence parameters.
Remove value cap from iteration; stop after raw first escape above100.
Replace bounded/unstable verdict with finite run status.
Subscribe calculations only to actual parameter changes.

records.boundary: These coordinate pictures reveal the selected sample. They do not establish manifold topology, a growth rate, or a global geometric property of the infinite sequence.
adaptation: Rename Topology control to Coordinates.
Start normalized triples at n3, excluding division by zero.
Remove unsupported roughly2n growth assumption; scale from finite ratios.
Use instanced meshes for the original addition/subtraction point clouds.

records.boundary: Reset and retention come from the programmed update rules. A circle does not itself force information loss, and this drawn helix is not a constructed Riemann surface.
adaptation: Give both modes the same accumulation rate μ per unit time.
Describe reset/retention as chosen rules, not consequences of topology.
Rename Riemann Helix to lifted helix in the exhibit.
Preserve paused trail, clear reset particles, and follow height with camera.

records.reason: The selected delay-coordinate version makes the coordinate choices explicit and matches the existing Recamán exhibit.
The mirror scan supplies the same finite prime-pair subject with clearer center–radius controls.
The High fit label is based on a count heuristic, not a goodness-of-fit test; resets alter the dynamics and the default can generate no bursts.

runtime.description: Local Atlas adapter preserving the selected supplied topic logic and visual concepts. Remote WH scaffolds and message bridge excluded.
runtime.requestPolicy: No runtime network calls; exhibit CSP connect-src none.
runtime.originalSourcePolicy: Only original topic scripts are published as text; the remote scaffold is retained in the supplied uploads, not executed here.
